Stacked on **#116** (`audit/sec-proposal-id-binding`), which is where proposal-id semantics live. Review that first; the diff here is the request-path half of the same subject.

This is the follow-up #154 named. #154 closed the `repoID` segment hole at every request site and left `proposalID` alone on purpose, because it is interpolated into the same two targets and needs its own format rule rather than the repo-id one.

## What is still open after #116

`proposalID` reaches the wire as a path segment at two endpoints:

```
GET  /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/proposals/{id}
POST /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/proposals/{id}/resolve
```

`newRequest` then attaches the member's bearer token, and the resolve body carries the member's whole fact set. `url.PathEscape` was the only thing between a caller-supplied id and that target, and it cannot perform this check: `.` and `..` are RFC 3986 unreserved, so `url.PathEscape("..") == ".."`, the `..` goes out on the wire, and any dot-segment-normalizing hop (net/http's `ServeMux`, nginx, a CDN, RFC 3986 §5.2.4) collapses the target onto a sibling route.

Demonstrated live against a real `http.ServeMux` — a proposal id of `".."` reaches:

```
ELSEWHERE-head:    /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts           (the fact-set head, Current's route)
ELSEWHERE-resolve: /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/resolve
```

Each with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` attached, and the second with the member's fact set in the body.

## Why #116 does not already cover it

`bindProposalID` constrains the id a **response** may carry — it refuses any served id that is not the value its own content derives, which is exactly right for the confirm-what-you-did-not-see problem #116 is about. It cannot constrain the id a **request** is built from:

- in `GetProposal` the path is assembled and sent *before* any response exists — `bindProposalID` runs on the decoded body, several statements too late to affect the target;
- `ResolveProposal` never reads a proposal back at all, so nothing binds `req.ProposalID`.

Today's in-tree flows happen to be safe, because the CLI resolves a human ref through `FindProposal` over a set that `ListProposals` has already bound, and a bound id is always `prop-` + 16 hex. That is a property of the call sites, not of the transport: `HTTPServer.GetProposal`, `HTTPServer.ResolveProposal` and `hostedbrain.Client.GetProposal` all take an arbitrary string and put it in a path. This is the "every call site remembers" shape #154 refused for the repo id.

## The rule, and why it is not `repoid.Validate`

Deliberately **stricter** than the one-safe-segment rule a repo id gets.

A repo id is an opaque server-issued value, so the most that can be demanded of it is that it stay one segment. A proposal id is not opaque: `ProposalID` derives it from the conflict's content, and #116's `bindProposalID` pins every served id to that derivation. So the set of ids this client can legitimately address is exactly the set `ProposalID` produces — `proposalIDPrefix` followed by `proposalIDHexLen` lowercase hex digits. Anything outside it is a target the member never had, not merely an awkward one, and loosening to the repo-id rule to share code would accept ids no legitimate flow can produce.

The rule is written against the same named constants the derivation uses, and `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` asserts `validateProposalID(ProposalID(p)) == nil` over a spread of proposals — so a change to the id's shape moves the rule with it instead of silently rejecting every real id.

## How the refusal is enforced

`proposalPath` is the only place a proposal id becomes part of a target, and it returns `(string, error)` rather than a string, so neither endpoint can build a path without handling the refusal — the same structural shape `repoBasePath` gives the repo id in #154. `ResolveProposal` builds it **first thing**, before the fact set is serialized at all: that body is the member's whole fact set, so the id that decides where it is POSTed has to be settled before there is anything to send.

A validated id equals its own `PathEscape`, so it is concatenated raw. `PathEscape` would be a no-op there, and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe.

## Tests

`internal/factsync/proposalid_segment_test.go`. Every test asserts the **resulting request** — the path that reached the server, or that no request was made at all. None compares an id against an escape of itself.

| test | asserts |
|---|---|
| `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` | the accepted set is the derived set; a derived id is one normal-form segment (by `path.Join`, not by an escape) |
| `TestProposalIDMustBeDerivable` | 26 hostile ids × both endpoints: refused with `ErrInvalidProposalID`, and **zero requests reach the server** — the token and the fact set never leave the process |
| `TestProposalIDLandsOnItsOwnSegment` | the exact target of both endpoints, the branch still in the query, and the path in normal form (`path.Clean` is a no-op) so no hop can move it |
| `TestProposalIDCannotReachAnotherRoute` | a real `ServeMux` with two handlers no proposal endpoint addresses. One subtest proves the collapse is real (the raw target does reach the fact-set head); the other proves the client will not build it |

`prop-x` / `prop-unknown` / `prop-missing` placeholders in the existing status-mapping tests become well-formed ids — those tests assert response-status mapping, not id shape, and a malformed id no longer gets far enough to have a status.

Orthogonal and non-overlapping: #154 validates the **repo** id at every request site, this validates the **proposal** id at the two sites that carry one. **Severity: MED (availability / self-DoS).** `brain_ingest_traces` accepted any path from the caller. A size ceiling does not bound a read: `open(2)` on a FIFO with no writer blocks *inside the syscall* before a single byte is read, and a character device yields bytes forever. Worse, the read happened **while holding the semantic index lock**, so one such call wedges the brain for every other caller — daemon, hook, and human alike.

**Fix, three independent layers:**
1. `os.Lstat` (never `os.Stat`) so a symlink pointing at a FIFO cannot slip through the type check a resolving stat would pass.
2. A post-open `SameFile` + `IsRegular` recheck, closing the regular-to-FIFO swap-during-open TOCTOU window.
3. A read deadline on descriptors that support one, so a pollable file that never yields EOF cannot park the caller. Regular files do not support deadlines and are unaffected.

Plus: the trace file is now read **before** the index lock is taken, so even a slow regular file cannot hold the lock.

**Tests (4):** FIFO rejected promptly; FIFO does not wedge the index lock; trace read happens before the lock is taken; regular-to-FIFO swap during open is rejected.

**Mutation-verified honestly:** disabling any *single* guard still fails safe — the other layers catch it, which is the point of defense in depth. Disabling **all three** fails `TestIngestTracesRejectsRegularToFIFOSwapDuringOpen` with `swap rejection error = <nil>, want it to name the regular-file requirement`. Reported this way rather than claiming a single-guard mutation proved the tests.

**Verification:** `go build ./...` clean; targeted FIFO/safe-read tests pass. This is the follow-up #154 named. #154 closed the `repoID` segment hole at every request site and left `proposalID` alone on purpose, because it is interpolated into the same two targets and needs its own format rule rather than the repo-id one.

## What is still open after #116

`proposalID` reaches the wire as a path segment at two endpoints:

```
GET  /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/proposals/{id}
POST /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/proposals/{id}/resolve
```

`newRequest` then attaches the member's bearer token, and the resolve body carries the member's whole fact set. `url.PathEscape` was the only thing between a caller-supplied id and that target, and it cannot perform this check: `.` and `..` are RFC 3986 unreserved, so `url.PathEscape("..") == ".."`, the `..` goes out on the wire, and any dot-segment-normalizing hop (net/http's `ServeMux`, nginx, a CDN, RFC 3986 §5.2.4) collapses the target onto a sibling route.

Demonstrated live against a real `http.ServeMux` — a proposal id of `".."` reaches:

```
ELSEWHERE-head:    /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts           (the fact-set head, Current's route)
ELSEWHERE-resolve: /api/v1/repos/{repo}/brain/facts/resolve
```

Each with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` attached, and the second with the member's fact set in the body.

## Why #116 does not already cover it

`bindProposalID` constrains the id a **response** may carry — it refuses any served id that is not the value its own content derives, which is exactly right for the confirm-what-you-did-not-see problem #116 is about. It cannot constrain the id a **request** is built from:

- in `GetProposal` the path is assembled and sent *before* any response exists — `bindProposalID` runs on the decoded body, several statements too late to affect the target;
- `ResolveProposal` never reads a proposal back at all, so nothing binds `req.ProposalID`.

Today's in-tree flows happen to be safe, because the CLI resolves a human ref through `FindProposal` over a set that `ListProposals` has already bound, and a bound id is always `prop-` + 16 hex. That is a property of the call sites, not of the transport: `HTTPServer.GetProposal`, `HTTPServer.ResolveProposal` and `hostedbrain.Client.GetProposal` all take an arbitrary string and put it in a path. This is the "every call site remembers" shape #154 refused for the repo id.

## The rule, and why it is not `repoid.Validate`

Deliberately **stricter** than the one-safe-segment rule a repo id gets.

A repo id is an opaque server-issued value, so the most that can be demanded of it is that it stay one segment. A proposal id is not opaque: `ProposalID` derives it from the conflict's content, and #116's `bindProposalID` pins every served id to that derivation. So the set of ids this client can legitimately address is exactly the set `ProposalID` produces — `proposalIDPrefix` followed by `proposalIDHexLen` lowercase hex digits. Anything outside it is a target the member never had, not merely an awkward one, and loosening to the repo-id rule to share code would accept ids no legitimate flow can produce.

The rule is written against the same named constants the derivation uses, and `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` asserts `validateProposalID(ProposalID(p)) == nil` over a spread of proposals — so a change to the id's shape moves the rule with it instead of silently rejecting every real id.

## How the refusal is enforced

`proposalPath` is the only place a proposal id becomes part of a target, and it returns `(string, error)` rather than a string, so neither endpoint can build a path without handling the refusal — the same structural shape `repoBasePath` gives the repo id in #154. `ResolveProposal` builds it **first thing**, before the fact set is serialized at all: that body is the member's whole fact set, so the id that decides where it is POSTed has to be settled before there is anything to send.

A validated id equals its own `PathEscape`, so it is concatenated raw. `PathEscape` would be a no-op there, and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe.

## Tests

`internal/factsync/proposalid_segment_test.go`. Every test asserts the **resulting request** — the path that reached the server, or that no request was made at all. None compares an id against an escape of itself.

| test | asserts |
|---|---|
| `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` | the accepted set is the derived set; a derived id is one normal-form segment (by `path.Join`, not by an escape) |
| `TestProposalIDMustBeDerivable` | 26 hostile ids × both endpoints: refused with `ErrInvalidProposalID`, and **zero requests reach the server** — the token and the fact set never leave the process |
| `TestProposalIDLandsOnItsOwnSegment` | the exact target of both endpoints, the branch still in the query, and the path in normal form (`path.Clean` is a no-op) so no hop can move it |
| `TestProposalIDCannotReachAnotherRoute` | a real `ServeMux` with two handlers no proposal endpoint addresses. One subtest proves the collapse is real (the raw target does reach the fact-set head); the other proves the client will not build it |

Orthogonal and non-overlapping: #154 validates the **repo** id at every request site, this validates the **proposal** id at the two sites that carry one. **Severity: MED (availability / self-DoS).** `brain_ingest_traces` accepted any path from the caller. A size ceiling does not bound a read: `open(2)` on a FIFO with no writer blocks *inside the syscall* before a single byte is read, and a character device yields bytes forever. Worse, the read happened **while holding the semantic index lock**, so one such call wedges the brain for every other caller — daemon, hook, and human alike.

**Fix, three independent layers:**
1. `os.Lstat` (never `os.Stat`) so a symlink pointing at a FIFO cannot slip through the type check a resolving stat would pass.

3. A read deadline on descriptors that support one, so a pollable file that never yields EOF cannot park the caller. Regular files do not support deadlines and are unaffected.

Plus: the trace file is now read **before** the index lock is taken, so even a slow regular file cannot hold the lock.

`bindProposalID` constrains the id a **response** may carry — it refuses any served id that is not the value its own content derives, which is exactly right for the confirm-what-you-did-not-see problem #116 is about. It cannot constrain the id a **request** is built from:

- in `GetProposal` the path is assembled and sent *before* any response exists — `bindProposalID` runs on the decoded body, several statements too late to affect the target;
- `ResolveProposal` never reads a proposal back at all, so nothing binds `req.ProposalID`.

Today's in-tree flows happen to be safe, because the CLI resolves a human ref through `FindProposal` over a set that `ListProposals` has already bound, and a bound id is always `prop-` + 16 hex. That is a property of the call sites, not of the transport: `HTTPServer.GetProposal`, `HTTPServer.ResolveProposal` and `hostedbrain.Client.GetProposal` all take an arbitrary string and put it in a path. This is the "every call site remembers" shape #154 refused for the repo id.

## The rule, and why it is not `repoid.Validate`

Deliberately **stricter** than the one-safe-segment rule a repo id gets.

A repo id is an opaque server-issued value, so the most that can be demanded of it is that it stay one segment. A proposal id is not opaque: `ProposalID` derives it from the conflict's content, and #116's `bindProposalID` pins every served id to that derivation. So the set of ids this client can legitimately address is exactly the set `ProposalID` produces — `proposalIDPrefix` followed by `proposalIDHexLen` lowercase hex digits. Anything outside it is a target the member never had, not merely an awkward one, and loosening to the repo-id rule to share code would accept ids no legitimate flow can produce.

The rule is written against the same named constants the derivation uses, and `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` asserts `validateProposalID(ProposalID(p)) == nil` over a spread of proposals — so a change to the id's shape moves the rule with it instead of silently rejecting every real id.

## How the refusal is enforced

`proposalPath` is the only place a proposal id becomes part of a target, and it returns `(string, error)` rather than a string, so neither endpoint can build a path without handling the refusal — the same structural shape `repoBasePath` gives the repo id in #154. `ResolveProposal` builds it **first thing**, before the fact set is serialized at all: that body is the member's whole fact set, so the id that decides where it is POSTed has to be settled before there is anything to send.

A validated id equals its own `PathEscape`, so it is concatenated raw. `PathEscape` would be a no-op there, and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe.

## Tests

`internal/factsync/proposalid_segment_test.go`. Every test asserts the **resulting request** — the path that reached the server, or that no request was made at all. None compares an id against an escape of itself.

| test | asserts |
|---|---|
| `TestProposalIDRuleIsTheDerivationRule` | the accepted set is the derived set; a derived id is one normal-form segment (by `path.Join`, not by an escape) |
| `TestProposalIDMustBeDerivable` | 26 hostile ids × both endpoints: refused with `ErrInvalidProposalID`, and **zero requests reach the server** — the token and the fact set never leave the process |
| `TestProposalIDLandsOnItsOwnSegment` | the exact target of both endpoints, the branch still in the query, and the path in normal form (`path.Clean` is a no-op) so no hop can move it |
| `TestProposalIDCannotReachAnotherRoute` | a real `ServeMux` with two handlers no proposal endpoint addresses. One subtest proves the collapse is real (the raw target does reach the fact-set head); the other proves the client will not build it |

`prop-x` / `prop-unknown` / `prop-missing` placeholders in the existing status-mapping tests become well-formed ids — those tests assert response-status mapping, not id shape, and a malformed id no longer gets far enough to have a status.

## Mutation

With `validateProposalID` neutered to `return nil`, both endpoints accept every hostile id and the route test reports the landing:

```
--- FAIL: TestProposalIDMustBeDerivable/GetProposal/dotdot
--- FAIL: TestProposalIDMustBeDerivable/ResolveProposal/dotdot
    ... (26 hostile ids × 2 endpoints)
--- FAIL: TestProposalIDCannotReachAnotherRoute/the_client_refuses
    proposal id ".." was accepted by ResolveProposal
    proposal id ".." moved the target and reached
      ELSEWHERE-head:/api/v1/repos/repo1/brain/facts with the member's bearer token
```

Validator restored: `internal/factsync` (122) and `internal/hostedbrain` (11) green, also under `-race`; `internal/cli` 2385 green. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l` clean.

## Relationship to #154

Orthogonal and non-overlapping: #154 validates the **repo** id at every request site, this validates the **proposal** id at the two sites that carry one. They meet in `httpproposals.go`, where #154 makes `proposalsPath` return an error and this adds `proposalPath` on top of it — a mechanical merge, whichever lands first.

**Severity: MED (availability / self-DoS).** `brain_ingest_traces` accepted any path from the caller. A size ceiling does not bound a read: `open(2)` on a FIFO with no writer blocks *inside the syscall* before a single byte is read, and a character device yields bytes forever. Worse, the read happened **while holding the semantic index lock**, so one such call wedges the brain for every other caller — daemon, hook, and human alike.

**Fix, three independent layers:**
1. `os.Lstat` (never `os.Stat`) so a symlink pointing at a FIFO cannot slip through the type check a resolving stat would pass.
2. A post-open `SameFile` + `IsRegular` recheck, closing the regular-to-FIFO swap-during-open TOCTOU window.
3. A read deadline on descriptors that support one, so a pollable file that never yields EOF cannot park the caller. Regular files do not support deadlines and are unaffected.

Plus: the trace file is now read **before** the index lock is taken, so even a slow regular file cannot hold the lock.

**Tests (4):** FIFO rejected promptly; FIFO does not wedge the index lock; trace read happens before the lock is taken; regular-to-FIFO swap during open is rejected.

**Mutation-verified honestly:** disabling any *single* guard still fails safe — the other layers catch it, which is the point of defense in depth. Disabling **all three** fails `TestIngestTracesRejectsRegularToFIFOSwapDuringOpen` with `swap rejection error = <nil>, want it to name the regular-file requirement`. **Severity: MED (memory exhaustion on a normal code path).** `refresh` slurped whole repo files into memory to hash them and scan for NUL. A high-signal doc over `max-file-bytes` is deliberately *kept* (marked truncated) with only its first `max-file-bytes` copied — so the read was unbounded even though the output was bounded. An ordinary refresh allocated the full size of the largest doc in the repo, attacker- or accident-controlled.

**Fix:** hash incrementally while detecting NUL in the same pass, so the recorded digest stays **byte-identical** and only one buffer is ever held. Manifest reads (`package.json`, `mise`) are bounded outright — a manifest is small, and a hostile or corrupt one should not exhaust memory before the parser sees it.

95 conversation https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/95#issuecomment-5448510574 Follow-up commit. An adversarial re-read of the first commit found two gaps and falsified part of what the original description claimed. Correcting both.

**1. Stored paths were not required to be canonical (MED).** Hashing `RecordID(Text, NormalizePaths(Paths))` let a record verify while *storing* paths the hash never saw — `NormalizePaths` drops syntactically invalid entries and truncates past `MaxPaths=2`, so a head record could carry e.g. `["a.b.c", "security.secrets.handling", "NOT A PATH"]`, verify against the id of `["a.b.c"]` alone, and then live under attacker-chosen taxonomy paths. Those stored paths are what listing, recall, and `activeConflictIndexes` read. `VerifyIdentity` now requires `Paths` to already equal `NormalizePaths(Paths)`. New test `TestSyncRejectsHeadFactWithUnnormalizedPaths`.

**2. `Sync` verified the head it read but never its own local facts before `Advance`.** The head check fails closed, so one malformed local record reaching the shared head breaks *every other member's* sync — the DoS lands on the wrong party. `Sync` now verifies `local` first and fails with a local-side error. New test `TestSyncRejectsUnpublishableLocalFacts`.

**Corrections to the original claims** — these were overstated and the code does not support them:

- *"a record that passes cannot have had its statement rewritten"* is **false**. `RecordID` hashes `NormalizeText`, which lowercases and collapses whitespace, so a statement can be re-cased or re-spaced freely under the same id. For a fact whose meaning turns on case (an identifier, a constant, a shell snippet) that is a real residual substitution. Closing it means changing `RecordID` and re-keying every stored fact, which is not this change.
- The provenance claim was **overstated**. `TestSyncRejectsHeadFactWithForgedProvenanceAnchor` only passed because the fixture also changed the text. Anchors sit outside the id, so a peer republishing a byte-identical statement can still attach an anchor naming a session it never saw — and can equally republish it with `Status=superseded` / `SupersededBy=<their fact>`, which suppresses the victim's fact for the whole team. **Every field outside the id — Status, SupersededBy, Kind, Locus, Confidence, RelatedIDs, Branch, Provenance — remains forgeable.** Authenticating those needs a signed record; the `brainwire` signing machinery exists but has no caller on this path yet. The test is renamed `TestSyncRejectsForgedStatementCarryingForgedProvenance` and documented to claim only what it proves.
- `readSharedFactHead` is **not** a hard security boundary: its error is swallowed as a warning at `facts_sync_cmd.go:157`. Verifying there is still correct (it is what feeds local proposal reconciliation) but `Sync` and `ResolveOpen` are the enforcing call sites.

`VerifyIdentity`'s doc comment now states the covered/uncovered surface explicitly instead of implying more.

Full suite green.
95 conversation https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/95#issuecomment-5448582426 Adversarial re-review. The check is real and the mutation holds (reverting the `sync.go` hunk fails `TestSyncRejectsHeadFactWhoseIDDoesNotMatchItsContent` and `...ForgedProvenanceAnchor`), and all three shared-head read sites are covered (`sync.go:91`, `proposals.go:400`, `facts_sync_cmd.go:349`). Two defects remain.

**1. BYPASS — the forgery this PR is named for is still reachable. `RecordID` commits only to `NormalizeText(text)` + `NormalizePaths(paths)`; every other field is unauthenticated.** Keep the victim's text and paths byte-identical (both are readable off the shared head) and forge `Status`, `Origin`, `SupersededBy`, `Confidence`, `Kind`, `Locus` or `Provenance` — `VerifyIdentity` passes and the record merges. forged.Status = factmerge.StatusRetracted
forged.Origin = "authored"
forged.Provenance = []factmerge.Anchor{{SessionID:"session-victim", CheckpointID:"cp-victim-1", Verified:true}}

- `readFilePrefix` preserves the truncation boundary exactly: a doc of *exactly* `defaultSeedMaxFileBytes` is still not marked truncated (`ReadAll(LimitReader(max+1))` yields `len == max`, and `len(data) > max` is false), matching the old `len(data) > defaultSeedMaxFileBytes`.
- `maxManifestBytes` is 16 MiB, so the new bound on `packageJSONCommands`/`miseCommands` refuses nothing real.

Two things.

**1. Conflicts with #131, which is not stacked on it and is not mentioned here.** Both are based on `main` and both edit `internal/cli/safe_read.go`:

```
git checkout entireio/audit/sec-trace-fifo-lock
git merge --no-ff entireio/audit/sec-seed-bounded-read
CONFLICT (content): internal/cli/safe_read.go     (import block)
```

Textually trivial. Semantically it deserves a decision, see below. The campaign has native stacks for `semantic.go` (#148), the HTTP chokepoints (#147) and `entityindex/build.go` (#142); `safe_read.go` is the fourth hot file and has none.

**2. This PR is about bounding a read over repo-controlled files, and it leaves the one read that cannot be bounded by a size ceiling.** `hashFileDetectingNUL` and `readFilePrefix` both call bare `os.Open`. `open(2)` on a FIFO with no writer blocks *inside the syscall*, before any ceiling can apply:

```
FIFO  O_RDONLY only        BLOCKED >2s
FIFO  O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK  opened, isRegular=false   (rejectable)
```

`inspectSeedFile` reaches it with no regular-file gate: it does `os.Stat` for the size (a FIFO reports 0, so it passes the ceiling), then `isLikelyBinaryPath` (name-based), then hashes. Reachability: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` does **not** list a FIFO, so a git worktree is safe — but `listSeedFiles` falls back to `filepath.WalkDir` whenever `git ls-files` fails (`seed.go:433-451`) and appends every non-directory entry, FIFOs included. So `entire-brain seed` against a non-git directory parks forever on one FIFO.

This is not a regression — `os.ReadFile` blocked identically — but this PR rewrites that exact line, and #131 adds `safeOpenRegularFile`, the helper that closes it. Whichever of the two lands second should route these two helpers through it (or add a plain `fi.Mode().IsRegular()` gate in `inspectSeedFile`), otherwise `safe_read.go` ends up with one hardened opener and two unhardened ones sitting next to it. Worth agreeing the merge order on the two PRs rather than discovering it in the conflict.

132 conversation https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/132#issuecomment-5458936883 Rebased onto #131 (`audit/sec-trace-fifo-lock`) to resolve the `internal/cli/safe_read.go` conflict, and retargeted this PR's base accordingly.

**Direction: #132 onto #131, not the other way round.** #131 owns the primitive — `safeOpenRegularFile`, the bounded open that refuses a FIFO or device. Everything this PR adds is a *reader built on top of* that primitive, so stacking it above #131 lets it inherit the bound instead of re-deriving it. The reverse order would have left #131 having to retrofit the two new helpers anyway.

Three things fell out of the merge:

- `safeReadFile`'s early size shortcut now runs on a descriptor `safeOpenRegularFile` has already proven regular, so its `fi.Mode().IsRegular()` test is redundant and is gone. The comment says why the reported size is trustworthy there.
- `readFilePrefix` and `hashFileDetectingNUL` moved from `os.Open` to `safeOpenRegularFile`. Both take repository file paths, which are exactly as caller-supplied as `safeReadFile`'s — and hashing a FIFO or a character device never terminates, which is the failure this whole helper exists to prevent.
- The streaming bound in `safeReadAll` stays the authority for a file that grows between the stat and the read; the shortcut is an optimisation, not the check.

Full `internal/cli` suite green.

https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/23
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Bind shared fact IDs to normalized text and canonical stored paths. Previously a peer could publish different text under another statement's ID, causing `Promote` to discard the original content and union its provenance onto the replacement.

`VerifyIdentity` rejects a mismatched content ID or noncanonical stored paths. `Sync` validates local records before publication and validates downloaded heads before merging. `ResolveOpen` and CLI shared-head reads validate downloaded records before proposal processing.

This is **content binding, not authenticated record integrity**. Case and whitespace substitutions remain possible because `RecordID` normalizes text. Status, superseded-by, origin, kind, locus, confidence, related IDs, branch, and provenance are outside the ID and remain unauthenticated. A valid ID does not establish that a retraction or provenance claim was authorized. Separate hosted Search/Get/MultiGet responses are outside this change. These limits and the recovery policy are documented in `docs/shared-fact-identity.md`.

Malformed shared heads fail closed. The client does not automatically discard records or rewrite a corrupted head; a hosted service operator must repair or restore it from a trusted source. This preserves the refusal boundary but does not prevent denial of service by a malicious shared-head writer.

Validation: factmerge, factsync, and hostedbrain tests pass after updating from main. Regression tests cover substituted text, noncanonical paths, and rejecting malformed local facts before publication. The forged-provenance test is explicitly limited to a fixture that also changes text; it makes no claim to authenticate anchors.
EOF
cat > /tmp/security5-131-body.md <<'EOF'
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/59
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A caller-supplied FIFO could block trace ingestion before any size ceiling applied, while holding the semantic index lock. `safeOpenRegularFile` now uses a nonblocking open on Unix and checks the resulting descriptor is a regular file. Symlinks to regular files remain supported; FIFOs and devices, including those substituted during open, are rejected.

Trace reading and parsing happen before acquiring the semantic index lock. The ineffective regular-file read deadline was removed: this is a file-type and memory bound, not a wall-clock guarantee for a slow backing filesystem.

#132 is stacked on this PR and uses the same opener for seed hashing and prefix reads.

Validation: focused safe-read, symlink, FIFO, trace-ingestion, and lock-ordering tests pass after updating from main. Tests exercise descriptor substitution during open and preserve ordinary symlinked inputs.
EOF

type repairRoundTripper func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error)
func (f repairRoundTripper) RoundTrip(r *http.Request) (*http.Response,error){return f(r)}

func TestProposalRepairDoesNotRetryPastCASConflict(t *testing.T) {
 t.Parallel()
 fake:=newHostedFake();srv:=hostedContractServer(t,fake);defer srv.Close()
 good:=OpenProposals([]factmerge.Proposal{{Action:factmerge.ActionMerge,CandidateID:"fact:a",TargetID:"fact:b",Branch:"main"}})[0]
 bad:=good;bad.ID="forged"
 fake.seed([]OpenProposal{bad})
 client:=&HTTPServer{BaseURL:srv.URL}
 preview,err:=client.RepairProposalIDs(context.Background(),"repo","main",false,"");if err!=nil{t.Fatal(err)}
 posts:=0
 base:=srv.Client().Transport
 client.Client=&http.Client{Transport:repairRoundTripper(func(r *http.Request)(*http.Response,error){
  if r.Method==http.MethodPost {posts++;fake.seed([]OpenProposal{bad,good})}
  return base.RoundTrip(r)
 })}
 if _,err:=client.RepairProposalIDs(context.Background(),"repo","main",true,preview.Ref);!errors.Is(err,ErrConflict){t.Fatalf("CAS race was accepted: %v",err)}
 if posts!=1{t.Fatalf("repair retried %d writes against unreviewed state",posts)}
 _,set,_:=fake.snapshot();if len(set)!=2 || set[1].ID!=good.ID{t.Fatalf("concurrent proposal lost: %+v",set)}
}
EOF

cat > docs/proposal-queue-repair.md <<'EOF'
# Repairing invalid proposal IDs

Hosted proposal listing and resolution reject IDs that do not match the decision
they name. A malformed entry blocks the branch's normal queue operations rather
than allowing an agent to resolve a substituted decision.

Use the explicit repair command to inspect the rejected entries without resolving
proposals or changing facts. The same hosted opt-in, no-egress, credentials, repo,
and branch settings as other `facts proposals` commands apply.

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --json
```

Review the returned `invalid` entries and save the output for diagnosis. To remove
only those malformed entries, copy the exact `ref` from that preview:

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --apply --if-ref '<preview ref>'
```

The command preserves valid proposals and never writes the shared fact head or
local fact store. Both the preview ref check and the server's compare-and-swap
must match. If the queue changed, preview it again; repair does not automatically
retry against entries that were not in the reviewed snapshot. Normal proposal
listing and resolution keep their identity checks; repair is an explicit
maintenance operation, not a verification bypass.

Missing IDs from older servers are derived as usual and are not removed. This
command repairs proposal ID/content mismatches only. It does not authenticate
provenance, repair malformed JSON, or repair a shared fact-set head.
EOF

# Next five security PRs

## Verification of the previous batch

GitHub marked #133, #118, and #158 merged. #156 and #157 remained open. Only #133 and #118 had landed on main: #158 merged into audit/contract-mcp after #118 had already merged, leaving #158's two-file change off main.

Repaired the landing path without merging any PR: merged audit/contract-mcp (including #158) and current main into #156, retargeted #156 to main, then updated #157 from #156. Both retain their own changes and the boundary error fix. Focused MCP tests passed after resolving the appended-test conflicts.

**With these current GitHub bases, merge #157 into #156 first, then #156 into main.** That carries #158 as well. Alternatively merge #156 first, then retarget #157 to main before merging it. Merely merging a child into an already-merged parent branch does not land its change on main.

## Selected PRs and dependencies

- #95 / Trail 23: shared fact content identity; base main.
- #116 / Trail 44: proposal ID/content binding; base main.
- #155 / Trail 76: proposal ID request-path validation; base #116.
- #131 / Trail 59: regular-file reads and trace lock ordering; base main.
- #132 / Trail 60: streaming seed reads; base #131.

All five were updated from their bases with normal merge commits and fast-forward pushes. Entire agent-help, checkpoint search, and file/line why context were consulted. Reviewed complete branch diffs, GitHub issue conversations/reviews/inline comments, and Entire findings including stale findings.

## Findings and disposition

### #95

The canonical-path check and pre-publication local validation already addressed two GitHub findings. Tests explicitly distinguish text forgery from unauthenticated provenance. The remaining overclaim in the PR description was corrected, and docs/shared-fact-identity.md explains the actual guarantee and recovery tradeoff.

This is normalized text + canonical path binding, **not full record authentication**. Case/whitespace substitutions and unauthenticated lifecycle/provenance remain possible; hosted Search/Get/MultiGet are outside this patch. Malformed shared heads still fail closed and require trusted service-side repair. Automatic dropping was not adopted because silently rewriting shared records can lose another member's facts. Merge judgement is for this accurately scoped hardening, not a claim that shared record integrity is solved.

The security monitor's score of 75 describes the critical content-forgery vulnerability being closed; its rationale does not identify a newly introduced defect. This score is retained in the evidence rather than treated as proof of full security.

### #116 → #155

Found and fixed a response substitution gap: GetProposal validated the response's own derived ID but did not require equality with the requested ID. Tests cover matching and substituted responses, including legacy omitted IDs.

Fresh Trail review then identified the poisoned-queue recovery gap (finding 01M2AMM8RQPJGG9J8DGD2AB87B). Added an explicit `facts proposals repair` preview and `--apply --if-ref` operation. It retains the rejected snapshot for inspection, drops only invalid queue entries, preserves valid proposals and facts, requires the reviewed ref, and uses server CAS without retrying against unreviewed state. Normal list/get/resolve stay fail-closed. The finding was resolved with commit/test evidence.

#155 retains its strict derived-ID format checks before constructing either single-proposal request. Updated it from the repaired #116 and tested the combined transport under the race detector. Its historical Windows failure log was no longer available; fresh CI replaces that obsolete run.

### #131 → #132

Earlier GitHub symlink and stack findings were already addressed: #131 checks the opened descriptor while allowing symlinks to regular files; #132 is stacked on #131 and uses the same opener in its readers. Removed #131's ineffective regular-file deadline and corrected the PR description: the guard bounds file type/allocation, not backing-filesystem latency. Trace reading/parsing still happens before the semantic index lock.

Reviewed #132's incremental hash/NUL scan, bounded manifest reads, prefix truncation, atomic output, and existing path guards. Resolved its import conflict while preserving the streaming readers and the updated opener.

## Validation

- #95: full `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.1 go test ./...` passed.
- #116: factsync and hostedbrain tests passed under `-race`; CLI proposal tests passed, including preview/apply and hosted/no-egress guards. Full suite is running on the repair commit.
- #155: combined factsync/hostedbrain tests passed under `-race` after inheriting the repair.
- #131: safe-read, symlink, FIFO, ingestion, and lock-ordering tests passed.
- #132: seed, bounded-read, safe-read, and trace tests passed.

Current-head CI and fresh Trail reviews/monitors are still being checked. Final readiness will be recorded below once they finish.

## Merge order with current bases

- #95 can merge independently.
- Merge #155 into #116, then #116 into main.
- Merge #132 into #131, then #131 into main.

If preferring parent-first merges, retarget each remaining child to main after its parent lands. Recheck CI on the resulting parent or retargeted child before landing it.
EOF",max_output_tokens:500}));

type repairRoundTripper func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error)
func (f repairRoundTripper) RoundTrip(r *http.Request) (*http.Response,error){return f(r)}

func TestProposalRepairDoesNotRetryPastCASConflict(t *testing.T) {
 t.Parallel()
 fake:=newHostedFake();srv:=hostedContractServer(t,fake);defer srv.Close()
 good:=OpenProposals([]factmerge.Proposal{{Action:factmerge.ActionMerge,CandidateID:"fact:a",TargetID:"fact:b",Branch:"main"}})[0]
 bad:=good;bad.ID="forged"
 fake.seed([]OpenProposal{bad})
 client:=&HTTPServer{BaseURL:srv.URL}
 preview,err:=client.RepairProposalIDs(context.Background(),"repo","main",false,"");if err!=nil{t.Fatal(err)}
 posts:=0
 base:=srv.Client().Transport
 client.Client=&http.Client{Transport:repairRoundTripper(func(r *http.Request)(*http.Response,error){
  if r.Method==http.MethodPost {posts++;fake.seed([]OpenProposal{bad,good})}
  return base.RoundTrip(r)
 })}
 if _,err:=client.RepairProposalIDs(context.Background(),"repo","main",true,preview.Ref);!errors.Is(err,ErrConflict){t.Fatalf("CAS race was accepted: %v",err)}
 if posts!=1{t.Fatalf("repair retried %d writes against unreviewed state",posts)}
 _,set,_:=fake.snapshot();if len(set)!=2 || set[1].ID!=good.ID{t.Fatalf("concurrent proposal lost: %+v",set)}
}
EOF

cat > docs/proposal-queue-repair.md <<'EOF'
# Repairing invalid proposal IDs

Hosted proposal listing and resolution reject IDs that do not match the decision
they name. A malformed entry blocks the branch's normal queue operations rather
than allowing an agent to resolve a substituted decision.

Use the explicit repair command to inspect the rejected entries without resolving
proposals or changing facts. The same hosted opt-in, no-egress, credentials, repo,
and branch settings as other `facts proposals` commands apply.

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --json
```

Review the returned `invalid` entries and save the output for diagnosis. To remove
only those malformed entries, copy the exact `ref` from that preview:

```sh
entire brain facts proposals repair --branch main --apply --if-ref '<preview ref>'
```

The command preserves valid proposals and never writes the shared fact head or
local fact store. Both the preview ref check and the server's compare-and-swap
must match. If the queue changed, preview it again; repair does not automatically
retry against entries that were not in the reviewed snapshot. Normal proposal
listing and resolution keep their identity checks; repair is an explicit
maintenance operation, not a verification bypass.

Missing IDs from older servers are derived as usual and are not removed. This
command repairs proposal ID/content mismatches only. It does not authenticate
provenance, repair malformed JSON, or repair a shared fact-set head.
EOF

import subprocess,json,concurrent.futures,collections
pairs=[(95,23),(116,44),(155,76),(131,59),(132,60),(156,77),(157,78)]
def read(pair):
 pr,n=pair
 d=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['entire','api','--to','cell',f'/api/v1/repos/{{repo_id}}/trails/{n}'],text=True))
 c=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['entire','api','--to','cell',f'/api/v1/repos/{{repo_id}}/trails/{n}/reviews/comments?stale=any&status=open&limit=1000'],text=True))
 checks=json.loads(subprocess.run(['gh','pr','checks',str(pr),'--json','name,state,link'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
 for label,data in [('trail',d),('comments',c),('ci',checks)]:open(f'/tmp/security5-status-{pr}-{label}.json','w').write(json.dumps(data,indent=2))
 return dict(pr=pr,head=d['headSha'][:8],comments=[(x['severity'],x['body']) for x in c['comments']],runners={r['runnerId']:r['outcome'] or r['state'] for r in d['runners'] if r['runnerId'] not in ['trail-summary','trail-semantic-diff']},ci=dict(collections.Counter(x['state'] for x in checks if x['name']!='Entire Gates')),failures=[x for x in checks if x['name']!='Entire Gates' and x['state'] in ['FAILURE','CANCELLED','TIMED_OUT']],gates={g['gateKey']:g['status'] for g in d['gates']})
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
 for d in pool.map(read,pairs):print(json.dumps(d),flush=True)
entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-brain  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

`ENTIRE_API_URL` (and the `--api-url` flag that overrides it) had **no scheme floor and no host allowlist**. Any value it was given received brain content — and the member's bearer token — in the clear. This adds a single shared validator (`internal/apiurl`) that requires `https://`, carves out loopback for local dev, and fails closed on everything else.

## What actually egressed over `http://` today (measured, not asserted)

I stood up a plaintext HTTP server bound to a **non-loopback** address (this machine's LAN IP, `192.168.1.121`), pointed `ENTIRE_API_URL` at it, and drove the real `publish` and `facts sync` code paths on the pre-fix tree. Both succeeded. Captured:

**`entire brain publish` → `POST http://192.168.1.121:PORT/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/artifacts`**

```
Authorization: "Bearer SECRET-BEARER-TOKEN-abc123"     <-- token crosses plaintext: YES
body: 2437 bytes, 4 artifacts
  kind=manifest  ref=<HEAD sha>   -> repo_key "gh/example/repo", default_branch, generated_at,
                                     provider/provider_version, and the full content index:
                                     sha256 digests, sizes, media types and on-disk PATHS of every
                                     snapshot / overlay / facts blob
  kind=snapshot  ref=<commit>     -> semantic snapshot NDJSON: {"symbol":"Foo","kind":"func"}
  kind=overlay   ref=<base>..<head> -> {"base":...,"head":...,"branch":"feature/x"}
  kind=facts     ref=main         -> durable fact text: {"branch":"main","text":"the repo uses go"}
```

**`entire brain facts sync --facts-backend http` → three plaintext calls, all bearing the token**

```
GET  .../api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts?branch=main            Authorization: Bearer <token>
POST .../api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts/advance                Authorization: Bearer <token>
     body.data (303 bytes) = the merged fact-set NDJSON, in the clear:
       {"id":"fact:60e95c57ed6370b3f79e74a5","paths":["ops.deploy.secret"],
        "text":"the prod deploy key lives in vault path kv/prod/deploy","branch":"main",
        "origin":"distilled","status":"active","provenance":[{"session_id":"session-EV"}],
        "created_at":...,"updated_at":...}
GET  .../api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts/proposals?branch=main  Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

So: **the whole brain artifact bundle, the merged durable fact-set (fact text, paths, provenance session ids), and the bearer token all crossed plaintext to an arbitrary attacker-named host.** `internal/cli/publish_test.go` already did `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_API_URL", server.URL)` against an `httptest` (plain http) server — the plaintext path was live and exercised.

Two aggravating details found while verifying:

- The refusal for a malformed URL happened *after* the whole bundle was built. `publish.go`'s own doc comment promises a refusal "BEFORE any resolution, disk read, or HTTP request"; with `ENTIRE_API_URL=http://evil.example` the pre-fix run got as far as `no brain found for this repo`, i.e. it had already resolved storage and read local state for an unsafe target.
- Non-HTTP schemes were passed straight to `http.Client` — `ftp://`, `file:///etc/passwd`, `//api.entire.io` and bare `api.entire.io` all produced a built request and a confusing transport error rather than a config refusal.

## The fix

New `internal/apiurl` — one validator, no I/O of any kind (no DNS, no disk, no network), so callers run it as their first act after resolving the flag/env and every refusal is egress-free:

- `https://` — always allowed.
- `http://` — allowed **only** when the URL's literal host is loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, `localhost`). This is what local dev and every `httptest`-based test in the repo use, so they keep passing unchanged. The name carve-out is exactly `localhost`, matching the plugin's existing `isLoopbackHTTPURL` check for the local model server; `api.localhost` is RFC 6761 loopback in principle but resolver-dependent in practice, so it takes the opt-in.
- `http://` anywhere else — refused (`insecure_api_url:`) unless the new documented opt-in **`ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_INSECURE_API_URL`** is explicitly truthy.
- Anything else — empty, relative, schemeless, protocol-relative, `ftp`, `file`, garbage — refused (`invalid_api_url:`), and the opt-in does **not** rescue it.

Loopback is decided from the URL's literal host only. No DNS: resolving would be a TOCTOU check, would need the network to validate a URL, and would let a hostile DNS answer widen the carve-out.

**Fail-closed direction.** `ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_INSECURE_API_URL` uses the *opt-in* spelling — only `1/true/yes/on/enable/enabled` unlocks plaintext; anything unrecognized (a typo'd `ture`) leaves the floor in place, with a deduped stderr warning so the operator learns their value was not understood. This is deliberately the mirror image of `securityToggleEnabled` / `toggleOn`, which fail an unrecognized value **ON**: those switch a protection *on*, so a typo must not disable it; this one switches a protection *off*, so the same fail-closed principle resolves the other way. It matches the existing `ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_HOSTED` publish opt-in.

Wired at every site that accepts a base URL:

| site | where |
|---|---|
| `internal/cli/publish.go` | right after the base URL is resolved — before `repoStoragePaths`, before the brain is read, before the bundle is built. Restores the doc-comment promise. |
| `internal/cli/facts_sync_cmd.go` | in the `http` fact backend resolution, before the backend is constructed. |
| `internal/cli/facts_proposals_cmd.go` | in `resolveHostedProposalTarget`, which is documented to make no network call. |
| `internal/factsync/httpserver.go` | in `newRequest`, the single request chokepoint for **both** `httpserver.go` (fact-set `Current`/`Advance`) and `httpproposals.go` (list/get/publish/resolve). Defense in depth: a caller that bypasses the CLI is still covered. |
| `internal/hostedbrain/client.go` | in `rpc`, the hosted MCP query chokepoint, next to the existing no-egress gate. |

`Validate` is idempotent, so the CLI-level check and the transport-level check compose without changing or re-rejecting the value.

## Tests (failing-first, then mutation-verified)

Written and shown failing against the pre-fix tree, then made to pass:

- `internal/cli/https_floor_test.go` — `ENTIRE_API_URL=http://evil.example` is refused for `publish`, `facts sync`, and `facts proposals`; each asserts the error is *not* a dial/DNS error, which would prove a request had already been attempted (pre-fix, `facts sync` and `facts proposals` failed exactly that way: `dial tcp: lookup evil.example: no such host`). Also: publish refuses **before** the disk read (it must not reach `no brain found`); the malformed-URL table; and the carve-out fence — loopback v4/v6/`localhost` stay allowed, the opt-in works, and a garbage opt-in value fails closed.
- `internal/factsync/https_floor_test.go` — `Current`, `Advance`, `ListProposals`, `PublishProposals` all refuse, with a counting `http.RoundTripper` proving **zero** requests reached the transport; loopback still round-trips.
- `internal/hostedbrain/https_floor_test.go` — same, for `CallTool`.
- `internal/apiurl/apiurl_test.go` — the validator table (schemes, loopback literals, `localhost` subdomains and lookalikes, opt-in truthiness incl. fail-closed garbage, malformed input), idempotence, and `IsLoopbackHost`.

Mutation check: with the floor neutered, the refusal tests fail; restored, they pass.

## Compatibility

- Every existing `httptest`-based test passes unchanged — they bind `127.0.0.1`, which is the loopback carve-out.
- Local dev against `http://localhost:8787` is unaffected.
- Breaking only for an operator pointing at a non-loopback plaintext endpoint, who now gets a clear error naming the opt-in.
- `--api-url` help text, the `publish` long help, and the README env table document the floor and the new variable.

## Green gate

`gofmt -l .` empty · `go vet ./...` · `go build ./...` · `go test ./internal/cli/... ./internal/factsync/... ./internal/hostedbrain/... ./internal/apiurl/...`

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Finding

Two production HTTP clients fell back to `http.DefaultClient`, which has **no timeout**:

- `internal/hostedbrain/client.go:55-60` — used by every hosted-brain RPC (`rpc`, and through it `Initialize`/`ListTools`/`CallTool`/`Search`/`Get`/`MultiGet`/`Status`).
- `internal/factsync/httpserver.go:39-44` — used by `Current`, `Advance`, and all four proposal calls in `httpproposals.go`.

The factsync one is **live today**, not only on the P1 hosted path: `internal/cli/facts_sync_cmd.go:573` constructs `&factsync.HTTPServer{BaseURL: baseURL, Token: token}` with no `Client`, so `entire brain facts sync --backend http` ran on an untimed client on both its read and its write path.

The realistic caller is the CLI or the workspace daemon passing `context.Background()`. With no caller deadline, the client's own bound is the only thing that can end the call.

## Proof

A test server that accepts the request and never responds, called with `context.Background()`:

```
--- FAIL: TestZZProveHang (20.00s)
    HUNG: no return after 20.002033333s against a wedged endpoint (http.DefaultClient has no Timeout)
--- FAIL: TestZZProveHangFactsync (20.00s)
    HUNG: no return after 20.002050125s (http.DefaultClient has no Timeout)
```

Both calls never return. The endpoint completes the TCP dial and only then stalls, so a dial-phase bound would not have helped either — the bound has to cover the wait for the response, which `http.Client.Timeout` does.

## Audit of every HTTP client construction (non-test)

| site | bound before | action |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/hostedbrain/client.go:59` | none (`http.DefaultClient`) | **fixed** — 60s |
| `internal/factsync/httpserver.go:43` | none (`http.DefaultClient`) | **fixed** — 5m |
| `internal/cli/publish.go:543` | `Timeout: publishRequestTimeout` (5m) | already bounded |
| `internal/cli/embed_ollama.go:73` | `Timeout: 60s` + loopback-only dialer | already bounded |
| `internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:1992` | `Timeout: timeout` + loopback-only dialer | already bounded |

No `http.Get`/`http.Post`/`http.Head` call sites and no other `&http.Client{}` exist outside tests.

## Fix

Each package gets a documented default bound and keeps the caller-supplied-client override:

- `hostedbrain`: 60s. The hosted tools are bounded reads (search / get / status).
- `factsync`: 5m. `Advance` uploads the whole merged fact-set, so the bound matches the five minutes the hosted publish path already allows for a body-carrying request (`cli.publishRequestTimeout`) rather than a short read timeout.

Both are plain `http.Client.Timeout`, the same shape `publish.go` already uses, so `http.DefaultTransport` and its connection pool stay shared. Both are `var`, not `const`, so tests can shorten them.

An earlier draft also set `Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout` on a cloned transport; that was dropped after it was measured to cause connection churn and ephemeral-port exhaustion in the existing suite. `Client.Timeout` already covers the response wait, which is the property under test.

## Tests

Per package: a direct assertion that the default client carries a non-zero `Timeout` (and that a caller-supplied client still wins), plus a behavioural test driving a wedged server with `context.Background()` and asserting the call returns.

Mutation-verified: restoring `return http.DefaultClient` in each package fails all four tests (the behavioural ones by hanging out their 15s budget); restoring the fix passes them.

## Verification

`gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` clean, `go test ./internal/hostedbrain/ ./internal/factsync/` green over 4 consecutive runs, `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Publish|FactsSync'` green.", "headRefName": "audit/sec-http-timeout", "headRefOid": "4e2984b9317cff92776fec7e71d81bdaf901090b", "title": "fix(hostedbrain,factsync): bound the default HTTP client", "url": "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/121"}

Stacked on #119 (`audit/sec-repoid-escape`), which is itself stacked on #137 → #121 → #125. Review after those; the diff against #119 is the four remaining request sites plus the package move.

## What was still open

#119 fixed one request builder — `hostedbrain.Client.rpc` — and deliberately left the identical hole at the other four to avoid cross-PR conflicts. Each of them interpolated a caller-influenced repo id into its target with `url.PathEscape` and nothing else:

| site | target |
|---|---|
| `factsync.Current` | `/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts` |
| `factsync.Advance` | `/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts/advance` |
| `factsync` proposals (`proposalsPath`, 4 endpoints) | `/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts/proposals[/{pid}[/resolve]]` |
| `cli.postBrainArtifacts` | `/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/artifacts` |

Escaping is not the rule. `.` and `..` are RFC 3986 unreserved, so `url.PathEscape("..") == ".."`, the `..` goes out on the wire, and any dot-segment-normalizing hop collapses the target onto a sibling route.

All four are real holes, demonstrated live against an `http.ServeMux` with the validator disabled — a repo id of `".."` reaches:

```
ELSEWHERE:/api/v1/brain/facts            auth=Bearer secret
ELSEWHERE:/api/v1/brain/facts/advance    auth=Bearer secret
ELSEWHERE:/api/v1/brain/facts/proposals  auth=Bearer secret
ELSEWHERE:/api/v1/brain/artifacts        auth=Bearer secret
```

Each with the bearer token attached, and on the write paths with the member's whole fact set or brain bundle in the body. Nothing upstream constrains the id: `--repo-id` / `ENTIRE_REPO_ID` is only checked for emptiness in `runPublish`, `facts sync` and `facts proposals`.

## Where the validator lives, and why

`internal/repoid` — a new leaf package, standard library only.

Three packages build `/api/v1/repos/{id}/…` targets and carry a bearer token on them: `internal/hostedbrain`, `internal/factsync`, `internal/cli`. They cannot share the rule through each other:

- `internal/hostedbrain` **already imports** `internal/factsync` (`hostedbrain.Client` drives the proposal endpoints over `factsync.HTTPServer`), so `factsync` importing `hostedbrain` back is an **import cycle**, not merely bad layering. The rule physically cannot live in either client.
- `internal/cli` sits above both, so putting it there is upside down.

A rule about the wire format shared by clients at three different layers belongs below all of them. `internal/httpx` (#121) is the same shape for the outbound HTTP policy those same three callers share, so this follows an existing precedent rather than inventing one.

`validRepoID` → `repoid.Validate`, `ErrInvalidRepoID` → `repoid.ErrInvalid`; the rule and its reasoning are unchanged, and #119's call site and test move over. One implementation, not three copies.

## How the refusal is enforced

- **factsync**: one helper, `repoBasePath`, is the only place a repo id becomes part of a target. It returns `(string, error)` rather than a string, so no endpoint can build a path without handling the refusal. `proposalsPath` is built on it, covering all four proposal endpoints at once. `ResolveProposal` checks first thing, before the fact set is serialized at all.
- **cli**: `postBrainArtifacts` checks at the chokepoint — it is the only function that turns an id into a network target and is reachable from callers that did not come through the command. `runPublish` also checks next to the `apiurl.Validate` floor, so a malformed target fails before any git or disk work, with the whole brain still local.

Validated ids equal their own escaped form, so the id is concatenated raw at each site: `PathEscape` would be a no-op, and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe.

## Tests

Every test asserts the **resulting request** — the path that reached the server, or that no request was made at all. None compares an id against `url.PathEscape` of itself, which is the tautology that let this survive the first fix.

| file | tests |
|---|---|
| `internal/repoid/repoid_test.go` | `TestPathEscapeIsNotTheRule` (pins the premise: the escaped dot segments still yield a rewritable path), `TestValidateRejects`, `TestValidateAcceptsAndYieldsNormalFormSegment` |
| `internal/factsync/repoid_segment_test.go` | `TestFactsyncRepoIDMustBeOneSafeSegment` (6 endpoints × 14 hostile ids, asserting zero requests reach the server), `TestCurrentLandsOnTheIntendedPath`, `TestAdvanceLandsOnTheIntendedPath`, `TestProposalEndpointsLandOnTheIntendedPath`, `TestFactsyncRepoIDCannotReachAnotherRoute` |
| `internal/cli/publish_repoid_segment_test.go` | `TestPostBrainArtifactsRejectsRepoIDThatIsNotOneSafeSegment`, `TestPostBrainArtifactsLandsOnTheIntendedPath`, `TestPublishCannotReachAnotherRoute`, `TestRunPublishRefusesBadRepoIDBeforeTouchingDisk` |

The `LandsOnTheIntendedPath` tests also assert the path is in normal form (`path.Clean` is a no-op on it), which is the property that makes it un-rewritable by any hop between the client and the handler.

## Mutation check

With `repoid.Validate` neutered to `return nil`, every site's test fails:

```
--- FAIL: TestPathEscapeIsNotTheRule
--- FAIL: TestValidateRejects
--- FAIL: TestRPCRejectsRepoIDThatIsNotOneSafeSegment          (hostedbrain, from #119)
--- FAIL: TestRPCCannotReachAnotherRoute                       (hostedbrain, from #119)
--- FAIL: TestFactsyncRepoIDMustBeOneSafeSegment
--- FAIL: TestFactsyncRepoIDCannotReachAnotherRoute
--- FAIL: TestPostBrainArtifactsRejectsRepoIDThatIsNotOneSafeSegment
--- FAIL: TestPublishCannotReachAnotherRoute
--- FAIL: TestRunPublishRefusesBadRepoIDBeforeTouchingDisk
```

Validator restored, all green: `internal/repoid`, `internal/hostedbrain`, `internal/factsync`, `internal/factgitmeta` (225 + 8 tests, also under `-race`), `internal/cli` (2434 tests; the publish subset under `-race`). `gofmt -s` clean, `go vet ./...` clean.

## Deliberately out of scope

`proposalID` is interpolated into the same two paths (`.../proposals/{pid}` and `.../proposals/{pid}/resolve`) and has the identical dot-segment hazard. It is left as `url.PathEscape(proposalID)` here because proposal-id integrity is #116's subject (`bindProposalID`), and a fix would have to decide the id's own format rule rather than reuse the repo-id one. Worth a follow-up on top of #116.

## The drift

Found by a live round-trip against the real entire-api, not by reading code.

The server now answers a violated cap with an actionable body:

```
400 {"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"branch is 600 bytes, limit is 512"}
```

The fact-set transport read only the status line. A member hitting a server-side limit got:

```
factsync: POST advance repo/main: unexpected status 400 Bad Request
```

No statement of what was wrong, and no statement of the limit. Six call sites dropped the body: `Current`, `Advance`, `ListProposals`, `GetProposal`, `PublishProposals`, `ResolveProposal`.

## What changed

**`internal/httpx/errbody.go`** — one renderer, next to the outbound HTTP policy the package already owns. Reading an error body has three hazards, solved once rather than at each call site:

| | |
|---|---|
| **size** | The body is not always the small envelope the endpoint documents. An ingress in front of entire-api answers 502/504 with an HTML page; a broken upstream can stream without end. The read is bounded (8 KiB) and the rendered line is bounded again (200 runes). |
| **shape** | JSON when the endpoint answered, HTML when something in front of it did. A gateway page says everything it has to say in its `<title>`; the markup is noise. huma splits a validation failure across a generic `detail` and a specific `errors[]`, so both are kept. |
| **content** | The bytes are attacker-influenced and are about to be printed to a terminal, so control characters (ANSI escapes, NUL, newlines that would forge a log line) and invalid UTF-8 are stripped. |

A body with nothing to say renders `""`, and the suffix form then adds no separator — a message is never left ending in a bare `": "`.

**`internal/factsync`** — all six sites render the body. **`internal/hostedbrain`** — replaces an ad-hoc `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(…, 4096))` that pasted the raw prefix through. **`internal/cli/publish.go`** — `publishServerDetail` delegates to the shared renderer (it handled huma's envelope correctly and pasted every other shape through as a raw 200-byte slice), and the 503 branch stops dropping the body: the server uses 503 for several distinct reasons and its own sentence is the only thing that says which.

## Semantics are pinned separately from the message

Every status this transport reads is load-bearing control flow. Each mapping has a test asserting `errors.Is`, not the string, so improving the message cannot quietly change the meaning:

- **412 / 409 → `ErrConflict`** — the CAS-loss signal `sync.go` and `proposals.go` re-read and re-merge on. Wrapped with `%w`; a bare 412 (no body) returns the bare sentinel exactly as before.
- **404 / 501 / 503 on the proposal endpoints → `ErrProposalQueueUnsupported`** — "this deployment has no queue", which degrades to the local queue rather than failing a sync whose head-advance already succeeded.
- **404 on one proposal → `ErrProposalNotFound`** — the normal outcome when another member already settled it.
- **The transient-dial retry classifier (#137) is untouched** — it reads a transport error, which exists before any response does. A test re-proves both halves: a local port-table blip is still retried, a refused connection still is not.
- **`brain publish` error classes** (`publish_auth:` / `publish_rejected:` / `publish_unavailable:` / `publish_too_large:` / `publish_failed:`) are unchanged, pinned per status.

## Pre-validate vs surface

**Pre-validated: the branch cap (512 bytes).** The branch is known before a socket is opened, and the request that would learn the limit carries the member's bearer token and, on `Advance`/`ResolveProposal`, the member's whole fact set — a multi-megabyte upload posted only to be told the branch name was too long. The client refuses first, with the same two numbers the server states, at a single chokepoint (`requestTarget`) covering all six methods. `maxBranchBytes` states the residual risk plainly: if the hosted cap is *raised*, this client refuses a branch the server would now accept and cannot detect that on its own. That is accepted only because 512 bytes is far outside the range of any real branch name.

**Surfaced, not mirrored: the publish artifact count and manifest-reference count, and whatever the hosted MCP surface applies to its own branch argument.** The client has no independent basis for those numbers — unlike the publish body-size ceiling, which it must project anyway to avoid building a multi-GB buffer — so a guessed constant would refuse requests the server accepts. The server's own message wins there.

## 5xx and non-JSON

Both covered by tests, on all three surfaces. The surfacing is keyed on "not the success status", not a hand-listed set of 4xx codes, so a 500 with `{"detail":"fact-set store is read-only"}` reaches the member. A 4 MiB HTML error page arrives as `504 Gateway Time-out` and the whole error stays under 1 KiB, with no markup and no control bytes.

## Verification

- Failing-test-first on all three surfaces (stub renderer → assertion failures → implementation).
- Mutation-verified, each reverted independently:
  - drop the surfacing → all 6 factsync surfacing tests fail
  - 412/409 stops wrapping `ErrConflict` → the conflict-semantics test fails (and the pre-existing `TestHTTPServerContract` fails with it)
  - 404/501/503 stops wrapping `ErrProposalQueueUnsupported` → its test fails
  - 404 stops wrapping `ErrProposalNotFound` → its test fails
  - drop the branch pre-validation → the branch tests fail, the at-the-limit control still passes
  - httpx forgets HTML titles and sanitizing → the httpx, factsync and hostedbrain rendering tests fail
  - publish 503 drops the body again → its test fails
- `mise run lint` clean; `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/factsync ./internal/httpx ./internal/hostedbrain` green, plus `-race` on the three transport packages.

Stacked on #154 (`audit/sec-repoid-all-sites`), the tip of the #125 → #121 → #137 → #119 → #154 stack that owns `factsync/httpserver.go`, `factsync/httpproposals.go`, `hostedbrain/client.go` and `cli/publish.go`.", "headRefName": "audit/http-error-body", "headRefOid": "aa5d6fbaa6a63229c264d5f6dce10c48e7bfee34", "title": "fix(hostedbrain,factsync,publish): surface the server's error body instead of a bare status", "url": "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/159"}

Contract audit of the MCP tool surface, pass 2 — the description half. Two tools described behaviour their handlers do not implement.

Both matter more than usual: an agent picks a tool by reading these strings, and a separate unified-MCP layer is about to wrap this surface, so a wrong description propagates into consumers that never see this repo.

## 1. `brain_refresh` promised a worktree semantic index it never builds

The description said, flatly: *"Includes current worktree content by default."*

The `worktree` argument only ever reaches seed and docs. The handler leaves `semanticWorktree` false (`refresh.go:327` reads it, `mcp.go` never sets it), so the semantic index that `semantic=true` rebuilds is built from **committed HEAD**. The refresh command's own `RunE` carries the comment explaining why: *"--worktree belongs to seed/docs. A dirty semantic snapshot must be an explicit `brain index --worktree` operation."*

So an agent calling `brain_refresh(worktree=true, semantic=true)` — the exact combination the description discusses — was left believing its semantic index reflected uncommitted work. It did not.

This is the same drift that shipped in the README as `refresh --worktree` and was corrected in #141. The MCP tool string and the two docs paragraphs describing `brain_refresh` were not part of that fix; they are corrected here.

## 2. `brain_index_repository` claimed a refresh it refuses, and hid its gate

- **"Build or refresh"** — `runSemanticIndex` errors with `semantic index already exists; use --force to replace it` unless `force=true`. The default cannot refresh. (#118 flagged this and left it, on the grounds that the `force` argument's own text disambiguates. I disagree: the top-level description is what an agent reads to *choose* the tool, and "refresh" is the wrong verb at exactly that moment.)
- **Path scoping was undeclared.** The path is confined to the bound repository root unless `ENTIRE_BRAIN_MCP_ALLOW_ANY_PATH` is set, and a relative path resolves against that root rather than the working directory. This was the one path-scoped tool that did not name its gate inline — `brain_delete_project`, `brain_list_projects` and the workspace tools all do, after #133, so an agent that hits the refusal learns the knob from the surface it is already reading. It is documented in README and `docs/limits.md`, but not where the agent is looking.
- **`profile` asserted a closed list.** It claimed *"full, fast, or syntax-only"*. Nothing in this repo validates the value or knows the set — it is forwarded verbatim to the external provider subprocess, and the CLI flag help for the same field says *"e.g. full, syntax-only"*. I could not verify whether `fast` exists, so rather than pick a side I removed the authoritative framing and made the string say what the code actually does. Flagging the two help strings still disagreeing as a follow-up for whoever owns the provider contract.

## Tests that pin declaration to behaviour

`mcpRefreshOptions` is extracted from the `brain_refresh` case block with **no behaviour change**, purely so the claim can be pinned against the handler rather than against a comment.

- **`TestMCPRefreshWorktreeContractMatchesHandler`** asserts in one test that `worktree` reaches `seed.worktree`, that `semanticWorktree` stays false in the `worktree=true, semantic=true` combination, that the default really is `worktree=true`, and that the description says all of this. If `brain_refresh` ever does start indexing the worktree, the test fails and forces the description to move with it.
- **`TestMCPIndexRepositoryDescribesForceAndPathScope`** drives `mcpResolveIndexPath` — absolute path contained, relative path joined onto the bound root, env gate lifting containment — beside the strings that describe it, and fails if the description drifts back to "Build or refresh" or drops the gate name.

## Verification

`go build ./...` clean, `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestMCP|TestDocContract'` green (73 tests). Full suite not re-run on a loaded host.
